2609.21942.title: When Should a Failing Robot Ask? Initiating Corrective Human-Robot Dialogue from Audited Sensor Evidence
2609.21942.paper_summary: A robot that fails at a task faces the first decision in corrective dialogue: act on its own diagnosis, consult another onboard sensor, or interrupt a person. Choosing well requires knowing how much the robot's sensors reveal about the cause and how reliable the robot's own diagnosis is. We build a simulated benchmark in which every failure's true cause is known, because we injected it, and measure what each sensor reveals, with explicit checks against data leakage. Some failures are diagnosable from camera images; others only from the robot's force data (0.99 from force data, no image method above 0.55). We then test six open vision-language models. Their behavior tracks the surface of the prompt, not the evidence: moving the refusal option from last to first in the answer list collapses refusal rates from 78-100% to 0-6% in three of the six swept model-and-family pairs. Accuracy from frames stays at or below a majority-class baseline under every prompt variant, with or without worked examples, and stated confidence carries no information about correctness. Handing the same models the force data as ten lines of text produces the first above-baseline diagnoses, in four of the six models: much of the failure reflects missing sensor data, not missing ability. We pose the choice as a three-action decision problem, act, consult your own sensors, or ask a human, whose optimal policy follows from measured accuracy. The models do not follow it, and their ask rates ignore a fourfold change in question cost. One question to a human still lifts them from that baseline to roughly the answerer's own reliability (0.70-0.81 when they ask). The decision to ask should be tied to measured accuracy and stated costs, not to the model's confidence.
2609.21942.paper_summary_zh: 一個在任務上失敗的機器人面臨著糾正對話中的第一個決策：依據自己的診斷行動、諮詢另一個機載傳感器，或是打斷一個人。做出正確的選擇需要了解機器人的傳感器對原因的揭示程度以及機器人自身診斷的可靠性。我們建立了一個模擬基準，在這裡每一個失敗的真實原因都是已知的，因為我們注入了它，並測量每個傳感器所揭示的內容，並明確檢查數據洩漏。一些失敗可以從相機圖像中診斷出來；其他的則僅能從機器人的力數據中診斷（力數據的診斷準確率為0.99，圖像方法的準確率高於0.55的沒有）。然後我們測試了六個開放的視覺-語言模型。它們的行為跟踪的是提示的表面，而不是證據：將拒絕選項從回答列表的最後移到第一，會使六對模型和家族中的三對的拒絕率從78-100%降至0-6%。在每個提示變體下，來自幀的準確率保持在或低於多數類基線，無論是否有示例，並且所聲明的信心對正確性沒有任何信息。將相同的模型以十行文本的形式提供力數據，會產生四個模型中首次超過基線的診斷：許多失敗反映的是缺失的傳感器數據，而不是缺失的能力。我們將選擇表述為一個三個行動的決策問題：行動、諮詢自己的傳感器或詢問人類，其最佳政策源於測量的準確性。這些模型並不遵循它，並且它們的詢問率忽略了問題成本的四倍變化。對人類的一個問題仍然使它們從基線提升到大約回答者自己的可靠性（當他們詢問時為0.70-0.81）。詢問的決策應與測量的準確性和所聲明的成本相關，而不是與模型的信心相關。
2609.21942.author: Eshika Pathak et.al.
